correctness.rationale: For positive arm lengths an extremal boundary pair forces the unique minimax center, yielding a finite piecewise-affine center selection. Every selector has explicit coordinate functional bounds derived from the boundary Lipschitz constraints; integrating along any boundary segment proves the global inequality. At every distinct triple an explicit base datum and small positive perturbation achieve the bound exactly. Ordered-length reduction follows from monotonicity of the harmonic mean. Separately formulated linear-program checks (3220) agree, with exact rational attaining pairs (50) and 3013 other finite tests. These tests are not substitutes for the proof.

value.rationale: Determines intrinsic and sharp perturbation stability of the unique pointwise optimally regular scalar AMLE on the complete natural class of all finite weighted stars. It separates the one-input isometric extension property from the two-input amplification, identifies branching as the threshold (two arms modulus one; three or more strictly larger), gives the sharp equilateral factor two and exact arm-imbalance instability. This is a natural operator invariant, not an arbitrary finite slice.
